content.text:
Kane is green — the browser run confirms dark mode survives the reload.

**The cause:** `App.tsx:22` initialized the toggle with `useState(false)`. The theme lived only in React state, so every fresh page load reset it to light regardless of what you'd picked.

**The fix** (all in `target-app/src/App.tsx`):
- `readStoredTheme()` / `storeTheme()` helpers read and write a `kane-notes-theme` key in `localStorage`, each wrapped in try/catch — storage access throws outright when a browser blocks site data, and that shouldn't take the app down.
- The state is now seeded with `useState(readStoredTheme)`. Passing the function as a lazy initializer means storage is read once on mount rather than on every render, and the `.app` element gets the right `data-theme` on its first paint, so there's no light-mode flash.
- The existing effect that syncs `document.body.dataset.theme` now also calls `storeTheme(isDark)`, so the choice is written back on every toggle.

One thing worth flagging: this persists an explicit choice only, and the default for a first-time visitor stays light. If you'd rather have the app follow the OS setting until someone actively toggles, that's a different default — say the word and I'll make the stored value tri-state (`dark`/`light`/unset) with `prefers-color-scheme` as the fallback.
